reason: E2 shows that 1 at% Gd micro-alloying markedly affects glass formation in Pd–Ni–P, supporting the premise that Gd can improve GFA in a P-containing system. However, E1 only demonstrates that the base Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy can form an amorphous phase under rapid quenching, providing no direct evidence for the claimed mechanism of atomic size mismatch or for the predicted improvement in thermal stability upon reheating.
premises: Gd has a much larger atomic radius than the base elements in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20
Large atomic size mismatch introduces strain and geometric frustration that retards nucleation and growth
Micro-alloying with ~1 at% Gd can significantly improve glass-forming ability in a P-containing alloy
The improved glass-forming ability will manifest as a broader processing window and suppressed crystallization on reheating
